title: Orient landing: hero with scenario-driven tiles and contextual screenshot suite
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a refreshed landing 'orient' hero that introduces first-time users to the Redwood Inference product in a scenario-driven way. Deliverables: hero artboard (desktop/tablet/mobile), a set of 3 contextual scenario tiles (Prototype, Scale, Private/VPC), supporting step-matrix diagram (task-lattice), and a screenshot suite for docs and marketing that highlights console, API quickstart, and Dedicated capacity flows. Goal is to increase immediate clarity for engineers evaluating the product while providing assets that are production-ready for the upcoming 2026-03 landing update.
acceptance_criteria: Hero variations for desktop/tablet/mobile exported at pixel-perfect sizes and named for CDN ingestion (hero_desktop@2x.png, hero_tablet@2x.png, hero_mobile@2x.png)
Three scenario tiles with 2 copy variants each (technical and product-focused) and accompanying iconography exported as SVG and PNG
Task-lattice diagram that maps first 5 steps for each scenario; provided as an editable Figma file and a static SVG for docs
Screenshot suite includes annotated console, quickstart API, and Dedicated capacity panels with redaction for PII and CPU/GPU metrics mocked
All assets meet AA color contrast and include alt text drafts for docs
Design handoff notes with spacing system, breakpoint rules, font tokens, and microcopy strings included in the Figma file and Confluence PRD
comments: 2026-02-15 - Ava M: Kickoff with PM (Samir) and Growth. Agreed to focus on three scenarios instead of five to reduce scope and speed delivery.
2026-02-20 - Early sketches uploaded to Figma. Direction A: tactile tile grid; Direction B: progressive timeline. Team notes prefer non-linear task-lattice to show branching flows.

2026-02-26 - PM review (Samir Patel): prefer technical copy on homepage hero but keep a product copy variant for marketing landing. Samir asks that tiles map to existing console routes (console/new, console/dedicated, console/vpc).

2026-03-01 - Eng sync (Sophia Chan): stated constraints on live metric screenshots (no real customer data). We will use mocked metrics and an overlay watermark. Eng asked for separate asset set sized for i18n expansion.

2026-03-04 - Design critique: accessibility pass required. Liam to run color contrast checks and validate keyboard focus for interactive hero prototype. Action: add alt text and aria guidance in handoff notes.

2026-03-08 - Stakeholder demo: VP Product approved hero direction with minor copy edits. Marketing requested a static hero variant for A/B test (image-first) and a simplified illustration variant for blog headers.

2026-03-10 - Ready for engineering handoff: Figma file link and export tokens added. Next: export PNG/SVGs and upload to Drive, coordinate with ENG-4912 (frontend landing integration) and PM-1312 for release timing.
notes: Design decisions and trade-offs: choose a low-illustration aesthetic to keep asset weight small for performance; use SVG icons with fallbacks. Prioritize clarity for the three scenarios — prototype (fast start), scale (dedicated capacity), and private (VPC/on-prem). We'll ship two hero variants for A/B tests: 'Context-first' (tile grid + short copy) and 'Screens-first' (screenshot carousel).
next_steps: Finalize copy variants and microcopy strings (Liam)
Export desktop/tablet/mobile hero assets and optimized SVGs (Designer)
Prepare annotated screenshot suite with mocked metrics and watermark (Designer)
Coordinate release integration and CDN rules with ENG-4912 (Sophie)
Create A/B test plan with Growth (KPI: click-through to quickstart + session time)
risks: Mocked metrics must not resemble real customer dashboards; legal check required if uncertain
Internationalization: long copy may break tile layouts for DE/FR; reserve extra width for i18n expansions
Performance: hero SVG complexity could affect LCP if not optimized
design_notes: Use 8pt grid and tokenized spacing. Implement hero max-width 1200px with center alignment.
Iconography should be 24px baseline with 2 weight variants (filled/outline) for emphasis states.
Provide both SVG and PNG fallbacks; name assets with semantic keys and sizes (hero_context_1200x600@2x.png).
Include copy snippets in Figma component text layer for accurate translations and A/B copy swaps.
